'''Martha Merrow''' (born 1957) is an American [[chronobiologist]]. She currently chairs the Institute of Medical Psychology at [[LMU Munich]]. Her career focuses primarily on investigating the molecular and genetic mechanisms of the circadian clock. Since joining LMU Munich in 1996, Merrow has investigated molecular and genetic mechanisms of the circadian clock as well as daily human behavior and [[medical psychology]].

==Life==
Merrow was born in 1957 in Bloomfield, Connecticut and currently resides in [[Munich]], Germany with her two daughters.

===Education===
Merrow received her bachelor's degree in biology at [[Middlebury College]] in 1979. After working in a pediatric nephrology laboratory under Dr. Thomas Kennedy for five years, Merrow headed to [[Tufts University School of Medicine]] and earned her Ph.D. in [[Immunology]] in 1991. Later that year, she pursued her Post-Doctoral Fellowship in Chronobiology at [[Dartmouth Medical School]], which she completed in 1996.

==Career==
===Research===
Merrow is well known for her work on the entrainment of circadian clocks in both humans and the fungus [[Neurospora crassa]]. She has also worked to describe circadian clocks in mutant or model genetic organisms lacking clear circadian phenotypes. Merrow worked with colleagues [[Till Roenneberg]] and Anna Wirz-Justice to develop the Munich ChronoType Questionnaire (([[Munich Chronotype Questionnaire|MCTQ]])), which assesses human [[chronotype]]s. Those with early chronotypes may be referred to as “larks” while those with late chronotypes may be referred to as “owls.”<ref>{{Cite journal
 | author = [[Till Roenneberg]], Anna Wirz-Justice & Martha Merrow
 | title = Life between clocks: daily temporal patterns of human chronotypes
 | journal = [[Journal of Biological Rhythms]]
 | volume = 18
 | issue = 1
 | pages = 80–90
 | year = 2003
 | doi = 10.1177/0748730402239679
 | pmid = 12568247
| url = https://www.rug.nl/research/portal/en/publications/life-between-clocks(d4fcf07b-97b2-4d4a-b1fe-07596c20f5bf).html
 | hdl = 11370/d4fcf07b-97b2-4d4a-b1fe-07596c20f5bf
 | s2cid = 15655036
 | hdl-access = free
 }}</ref>

Merrow's molecular chronobiology lab at LMU Munich uses [[nematode]]s, yeast, fungi, and human tissue cultures to study the [[circadian clock]] in simple systems. Her research focuses on oscillations at the cellular and molecular levels as a representation of organismal rhythms.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imp.med.uni-muenchen.de/research/molecular_chronobiology-merrow/index.html|title=Molecular Chronobiology - Merrow Lab - Institute of Medical Psychology - LMU Munich|website=www.imp.med.uni-muenchen.de|language=en|access-date=2017-04-13}}</ref> Merrow's lab often uses techniques such as the insertion of Luciferase gene fusions or Green Fluroescent Protein to visualize oscillations of RNA levels, protein abundance, or protein modifications within the cell. Oscillations in the entrained phase can then be compared to the organism's free running period or the phase produced by other methods of entrainment to elucidate the mechanism of the clock.

=== Professional achievements ===
While she was a professor of Chronobiology at University of Groningen, Merrow led Sub-Project 4: Novel Clock Genes and Principles within EUCLOCK, a European organization of researchers interested in [[entrainment (chronobiology)|entrainment]] of circadian clocks.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.euclock.org/projects/novel-clock-genes-and-principles.html|title=Sub-Project 4: Novel Clock Genes and Principles|access-date=2017-04-27}}</ref> Merrow has served as the secretary and a member for the SRBR and is  currently the vice-president of the European Biological Rhythms Society (EBRS).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ebrs-online.org/board/category/board  |title=European Biological Rhythms Society board members|access-date=2017-04-13}}</ref> Merrow coordinated the OnTime consortium, a group consisting of Netherlands-based researchers in the field of chronobiology and is a member of the Program Committee for the upcoming XV EBRS Congress event to be held in Amsterdam.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nin-meeting.nl/index.html?org/org.html~mainFrame  |title=XV EBRS Congress information|access-date=2017-04-13}}</ref> The group attempts to improve health through an understanding of circadian clocks and their entrainment.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-martha-merrow/1163629|title=Prof. Martha Merrow - AcademiaNet|website=www.academia-net.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.clocks-ontime.nl/consortium.html |title=OnTime Consortium|access-date=2017-04-13}}</ref> This consortium has its roots in Merrow's organization of the Dutch Clock Club, which is based on the structure of the UK Clock Club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/med/news/events/ukclockclub/programme/ |title=Warwick Medical School Summer UK Clock Club Programme|access-date=2017-04-27}}</ref> She remains active in academia and has taught at the European Summer School for Chronobiology nearly every year since and including 1996. Additionally, Merrow strives to develop networks for women in science.

====Timeline of achievements====
*2004: Received [[Jürgen Aschoff#Aschoff's Rule (prize)|Aschoff's Rule]] prize from EBRS (European Biological Rhythms Society)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ebrs-online.org/awards/other-awards/aschoff-s-ruler |title=European Biological Rhythms Society|access-date=2017-04-13}}</ref>
*2004: Rosalind Franklin Research Fellowship at University of Groningen <ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rug.nl/news/2006/12/42_16 |title=University of Groningen News|access-date=2017-04-13}}</ref>
*2006: Became Full Professor of Molecular and Genetic Chronobiology at University of Groningen
*2006: VICI Award <ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/research-projects/i/26/2026.html|title=NWO Research Projects Keeping time: molecular entrainment mechanisms of biological clocks|access-date=2017-04-27}}</ref>
*2011: Awarded OnTime Grant <ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rug.nl/news/2011/05/stwsubsidiemerrow?lang=en|title=University of Groningen: Substantial grant from Technology Foundation STW for chronobiologist Martha Merrow|date=13 May 2011|access-date=2017-04-27}}</ref>
*2012: Became Chair of Institute for Medical Psychology at LMU Munich <ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.en.uni-muenchen.de/about_lmu/introducing-lmu/people/appointments/2012/index.html |title=LMU new appointments 2012|access-date=2017-04-13}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.imp.med.uni-muenchen.de/members/mitarbeiter/merrow1/index.html  |title=LMU medical faculty|access-date=2017-04-13}}</ref>
*2014: Produced a Coursera on Chronobiology <ref>{{cite web |url=https://tr.coursera.org/instructor/marthamerrow|title=Coursera: Instructor Martha Merrow|access-date=2017-04-27}}</ref>
